what: Every corpus sentence claiming that something is stated, recorded on every row, or shown, with the surface a person reads it on and the text that surface must carry.
whyItIsOwed: No check in this corpus reads a rendered page. Every one asserts over source, over the store, or over a document, so a claim about what a person can see is verified against what a machine can read. The gallery review showed what that costs: `reached-ceiling` recorded that it ran two of its three clauses, `check-completeness` confirmed the result was present, ARCHITECTURE said the narrowing is stated outright, and every one of those was true of the store while the screen dropped the note. Nothing upstream was wrong, so nothing upstream could have caught it.
whatItCannotSay: Nothing about whether a page is any good, readable, or well laid out. The one question is whether a corpus sentence asserting visibility is true of the thing a person looks at.
howAClaimIsRetired: A claim whose surface does not exist yet names the checkpoint that builds it and is counted out of scope, on the same terms an out-of-scope architecture claim is. It is not a permanent exemption: the count falls as checkpoints land.

claims.name: reached-ceiling-narrowing
claims.sentence: the check runs its two average clauses and is narrower than this line describes, which the setup record says outright rather than leaving to be inferred from a passing verdict
claims.why: The first of the two the gallery review found. The note was in the store and the screen dropped it whenever a value sat beside it, so the caveat was written down and never stated to anybody.

claims.name: calibration-market-cap-exemption
claims.sentence: every short verdict here says which clauses ran
claims.why: The second, and worse on the calibration side: every one of the 16,917 short rows carries the exemption note, and a reader paging them would have seen a four-clause verdict.

claims.name: every-check-appears-on-every-card
claims.sentence: Every check appears on every card, passed and failed alike, and a check handed nothing shows what was absent rather than a blank
claims.mustCarry: no stop or no daily range for the session
claims.why: A check handed nothing must show what was absent. A blank would read as a check that passed quietly.

claims.name: a-number-without-a-count-is-not-shown
claims.sentence: Every panel shows its own count. A number without one is not shown at all
claims.why: The failure this whole system exists to avoid is reading a pattern in forty observations, and a panel printing a figure with no denominator is the most efficient way to commit it.

claims.name: every-panel-states-its-population
claims.sentence: a figure states the population it was computed over, in the same breath, and a figure over a mixed population is not stated at all
claims.why: Band 1 is over every flagged setup and band 2's decile curve is over the capped candidates, and at the calibrated thresholds those differ by three orders of magnitude. Until 3.7 the page showed both without saying which rows either used, which is the fifth defect shape sitting on the surface the sixth is about.

claims.name: each-panel-carries-the-condition-it-reads-badly-under
claims.sentence: Each panel carries the condition under which it reads badly, because a scoreboard that can only show good news is decoration
claims.why: A band that could only report a result and never a non-result would be a page nobody could be disappointed by, which is the same as a page nobody should believe.

claims.name: long-and-short-are-two-blocks
claims.sentence: The two sides are two lists on the wire and two blocks on the screen
claims.why: The pooling rule is easiest to break on a screen, where one table with a direction column looks tidier than two blocks and quietly invites a total.

claims.name: borrow-assumption-on-every-short-trade
claims.sentence: Both will be recorded as unmodelled assumptions on every short trade, from 4.7
claims.why: The third the obligation names, and the one nobody had looked at. No trade row exists until 4.7 and no journal until 4.11, so the claim rests on a surface nobody has built. It was written in the present tense until 3.0(d).

claims.name: realised-risk-beside-intended
claims.sentence: the realised risk is recorded beside the intended risk on every position so the gap is visible rather than assumed away
claims.why: Same shape as the borrow assumption. Share counts round down and the gap that creates is a real cost, visible only if something shows both numbers.

claims.name: failed-checks-greyed-with-the-failing-check-named
claims.sentence: failed checks greyed with the failing check named
claims.why: A greyed row that did not say which check failed would tell a reader a name was rejected and nothing about why, which is the state the gallery was in before 2.9.

claims.name: loss-causes-as-a-share
claims.sentence: Failed setups shrinking as a share is direct evidence the filter improved. Noise stop-outs shrinking is evidence the execution improved
claims.why: Two different wins with the same symptom, and this is the only place that would separate them. The panel is on the page now declaring its checkpoint rather than absent.

claims.name: proposal-hit-rate-by-pack-version
claims.sentence: This is the project's stated success criterion made visible, from 6.8
claims.why: The only band that measures the AI, and it measures the evidence rather than the model.

claims.name: band-one-shows-how-far-off-the-answer-is
claims.sentence: Band 1 shows its raw count, its effective count and the minimum, every night, and checkpoint 3.6 fires on the third of those rather than on a date
claims.why: 3.6 used to wait three months, a figure written before anything was measured. It now waits for a sample, and a trigger a reader cannot see from the first night is a date in disguise. The store can hold all three numbers and the page is the only place the claim is ever about.

claims.name: a-panel-below-its-minimum-says-it-is-not-an-answer
claims.sentence: Below the minimum sample the panel is not yet an answer, and says so rather than leaving it to be inferred from a figure
claims.why: This is the state the panel is in for every night of the wait, and it is the state a reader is most likely to misread: a mean sitting there with an interval around it looks like a result. The sixth defect shape is exactly a claim about a surface verified against the store, so the words are asserted on the page.

claims.name: a-withheld-panel-says-which-shortage-is-blocking
claims.sentence: A withheld band 1 panel says whether it is short of sessions or short of evidence, because the two are settled by completely different things
claims.mustCarry: a shortage of sessions rather than of evidence
claims.why: Only one thing withholds a figure: the block bootstrap needs twenty sessions. The minimum sample is a separate statement about information, and the two can contradict each other, because a fortnight of very wide nights reaches the minimum before it reaches twenty sessions. Without this the page could say the minimum was reached beside a figure it was refusing to show, and a reader could not tell which was blocking or what would unblock it.

claims.name: a-withheld-panel-names-a-control-shortage-when-that-is-the-cause
claims.sentence: Where a side still has none, the band 1 panel is withheld and says a shortage of control outcomes is the cause rather than a shortage of time
claims.mustCarry: a shortage of control outcomes rather than of time
claims.why: ForwardReturnFiller wrote no control outcome for the whole of phase 3, so band 1 was withheld on every night with an effective count of nought, and 3.6 fires on that count. The panel said no session had closed a 10-session horizon while the store held thirty nights of closed horizons. The wrong cause is worse than no cause: it sends a reader to wait for something that has already happened. The stage's own words are held by the fixture at accumulation.starved.withheldBecause; this holds that the page renders them.

aSurfaceCanBePartOfAPageThatExists: Two of the deferred claims name a panel rather than a page. `/scoreboard` is built and both panels are on it declaring the checkpoint that fills them, so the surface a reader looks at exists and the thing it must carry does not. Naming the page alone would have made the out-of-scope line read "/scoreboard does not exist yet", which is false and is the kind of wrong reason that survives because nobody reads a passing check's detail.
